task.description: Run the full mix test suite as the authoritative pre-merge regression check for REQ-225.

result.note: Ran full suite in foreground with `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh && mix test` (docker postgres/keycloak containers were already up, started via sudo since this user's docker group membership isn't active in-session). Result: 3304/3306 passed (6/6 properties, 3298/3300 tests), 19 excluded; Failed: 2 tests. Suite took 1340.9s. Re-ran only the 2 failures via `mix test --failed` to capture full detail: both are in test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs ('a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row...' and 'a matching rust pin reports OK with no mismatch...'), both failing with `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)`. Confirmed `which rustc` / `rustc --version` -> 'command not found' in this environment -- rustc is simply not installed in this sandbox, not a code defect. Diff-scope check (`git diff main...HEAD --stat`) confirms this branch touches exactly lib/letflow/entities/definition.ex, lib/letflow/entities/definition/shape.ex, lib/letflow/entities/definition/validator.ex, test/letflow/entities/definition/shape_test.exs, test/letflow/entities/definition/validator_test.exs (plus design doc and handoff JSON files) -- letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs is NOT in that scope. This matches the environment/toolchain-mismatch flake class documented in docs/anti-patterns.md ('A batch of unrelated compile/tool-version failures ... check .tool-versions / mix letflow.check_toolchain ... especially in a throwaway/containerized verification environment that doesn't inherit the repo's own toolchain'). All REQ-225 entity-definition tests (shape_test.exs, validator_test.exs) passed with zero failures. Reporting status FAIL per instructions (any failure with an unfamiliar or unverifiable root cause is reported honestly rather than waved off) but attributing both failures to a missing rustc binary in this sandbox, not to REQ-225's diff -- RELEASE-VALIDATOR should independently confirm rustc availability in its own verification environment.
